title: A Local AI Lane for Contoso Consultants

slides.title: Local AI for Traveling Consultants
slides.subtitle: A second AI lane alongside Microsoft 365 Copilot
slides.notes: Today we propose a small, low-risk pilot: ten consultants, two weeks, a local AI lane on Surface Laptop Ultra next to the Copilot you already use.

slides.title: Consultants Live in Drafting Mode
slides.takeaway: Summaries are frequent, repeated and time-consuming for 1,200 consultants.
slides.notes: Of 4,000 employees, 1,200 travel. Each writes about six client summaries a week, roughly 25 minutes each. That is repeated, sensitive drafting work, exactly where a local assistant can help.

slides.title: From Interview to Client Summary
slides.takeaway: The drafting step is where consultants lose the most time.
slides.notes: The workflow is familiar: interviews, documents, then drafting. Drafting is the bottleneck and the step a local model accelerates.

slides.title: Local AI Is a Carry-On Bag
slides.takeaway: Your essentials travel with you, even when Wi-Fi does not.
slides.notes: About 30% of client sites restrict guest Wi-Fi. Like a carry-on, local AI goes where the consultant goes. Disconnected use is something we validate in the pilot.

slides.title: Two Lanes, One Consultant
slides.takeaway: Sensitive drafting stays local; Copilot keeps handling collaboration work.
slides.notes: This is hybrid. Copilot stays exactly as it is. The local lane adds a place for sensitive, repeated drafting where client documents never need to leave the laptop.

slides.title: Adding a Lane, Not Replacing
slides.takeaway: Hybrid keeps Copilot and adds on-device drafting for sensitive work.

data.verdict: Hybrid gives consultants the right lane per task

slides.notes: We are not replacing any subscription. The recommendation is a second lane for specific work, while Copilot keeps doing what it does well.

slides.title: Inside the Surface Laptop Ultra
slides.takeaway: Workstation-class hardware runs large open models right on the laptop.
slides.notes: The device pairs a Blackwell RTX GPU with 20 CPU cores and 128 GB of memory, enough to host a catalog of 28 open models locally.

slides.title: Fast Enough to Feel Instant
slides.takeaway: Large local models generate text faster than anyone reads.
slides.notes: On this device Gemma 4 26B decodes about 72 tokens per second and Qwen3-Coder 30B about 86. In fact, this deck was generated on this laptop by a local model with no cloud calls.

slides.title: Capacity Worth Measuring
slides.takeaway: Illustrative estimate only; the pilot measures the real number.
slides.notes: If a local assistant saved five minutes per summary, that is 27,600 hours a year of capacity. This is unvalidated and illustrative, not a savings claim. The pilot exists to measure the real number.

slides.title: A Two-Week Pilot Plan
slides.takeaway: Ten consultants, 14 days, three clear measures.
slides.notes: The pilot measures task time, draft quality and user experience, and validates disconnected use at client sites.

slides.title: Approve the 10-User Pilot

data.ask: Approve a 2-week, 10-user Surface Laptop Ultra pilot.

slides.notes: Our ask: approve ten users for two weeks. We return with measured results, then decide together on next steps.
